name: Extended Euclidean Bezout coefficient recurrence
definition: Initialize (r0,r1)=(a,b), (s0,s1)=(1,0), (t0,t1)=(0,1). While r1>0 set q=floor(r0/r1); replace each pair (u0,u1) by (u1,u0−q u1). At termination r0=gcd(a,b)=a s0+b t0.
variables: a,b nonnegative integers not both zero; r remainders; s,t integer coefficients; q quotient
assumptions: Exact integer arithmetic including signed coefficients
limitations: O(log(M+1)) Euclidean iterations for M=max(a,b)≥1; a constant number of integer registers, not constant bit storage. Signed coefficients and intermediate products require exact or checked arithmetic. Bit cost depends on arithmetic implementation; coefficients need not be unique or minimal. Not constant time
failure_conditions: Both inputs zero, invalid integer input or overflow.
computation: Update all three pairs simultaneously using the same quotient; return (r0,s0,t0) when r1=0. The zero-operand cases follow from initialization. Never divide by zero.

source.citation: Cornell University CS 2800, Fall 2017, Lecture 34: Properties of GCD, Bézout induction reviewed, https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs2800/2017fa/lectures/lec34-gcd.html ; iterative invariant and iteration bound independently derived.

required_inputs: Two nonnegative integers, not both zero.
mechanism_note: Variant of remainder gcd. Initially each remainder is its stated linear combination. Subtracting q times the second combination from the first preserves this invariant; the pair update has determinant −1. Euclidean termination and gcd invariance give the result. The remainder sequence is unchanged, hence the iteration bound still applies.

name: Segmented Eratosthenes prime sieve
definition: For each integer block [L,R] within [2,N], mark initially true; for each base prime p≤sqrt(R), clear indices beginning at m=max(p²,p ceil(L/p)) and increment by p until m>R.
variables: N inclusive upper bound; B positive block length; L,R inclusive block endpoints; p base prime; m first multiple to clear
assumptions: Exact integer indices and square-root bounds; complete base primes through floor(sqrt(N)); disjoint consecutive blocks of length at most B covering [2,N]
limitations: O(B+sqrt(N)) auxiliary words excluding streamed output (cap B at N). Simple per-block scanning incurs O(ceil((N−1)/B) π(floor(sqrt(N)))) overhead in addition to asymptotic O(N log log N) marking and initialization; π counts primes. Small B can worsen runtime. No cache performance claim
failure_conditions: Invalid block size, incomplete base primes or overflow.
computation: Compute base primes once using an ordinary sieve (empty when floor(sqrt(N))<2). For L=2,2+B,…≤N set R=min(N,L+B−1); allocate R−L+1 flags and clear as specified. Emit surviving L+i in increasing order, then discard flags. Use checked products and integer ceiling division.

source.citation: Kim Walisch, primesieve algorithm documentation, segmentation and square-start marking reviewed, https://github.com/kimwalisch/primesieve/blob/master/doc/ALGORITHMS.md ; simple unoptimized block recurrence and scan overhead independently derived. University of Illinois CS 491 CAP sieve transcript supports base sieve.

required_inputs: Integer inclusive bound N≥2 and positive integer block size B.
mechanism_note: Variant of Eratosthenes. Each cleared number is a multiple of p at least p², hence composite. Every composite in a block has a least prime factor p≤sqrt(R) and lies at or beyond both start thresholds. No prime is cleared. The blocks partition the range, preserving the same prime set. Marking uses the standard prime reciprocal bound; scanning base-prime lists adds overhead.
